# Orbweaver — Enforcement Registry: Active Gates

**GENERATED by `pnpm exec node tooling/src/verify/cli.ts baseline active-gates-index`** — do not hand-edit the table or the count below; edit this
generator and regenerate. Everything else on this page is authored here too, so a change to the prose
is a change to the generator's source, never a diff against the committed file.

> Maintained tools own the claims they can express: Biome, ESLint, the compiler and dependency-cruiser.
> Structural gates retain unmatched semantic judgments and consume shared code facts.
> A gate proposed but not yet buildable is a `docs/work` decision item; a gate
> proposal turned down stays as a rejected ADR (for example `docs/adr/0220-rejected-neo-and-report-only-gates.md`).

Gates are written before the code they govern, so code is born compliant. A gate that would only
false-fire on a placeholder tree is not missing — it is a `docs/work` item, keyed to the code that
makes it meaningful.

A property with no gate of its matching name is not automatically a gap: ask which tier of this ladder
already holds it before filing one. A control-flow or per-request property (an insert-then-fan-out
ordering, an owner-scoped route) is routinely held by a behavioural suite by design, one tier below a
structural gate, and a resolve-time or lint-time fact (the package cake, dependency-cruiser) can hold a
property a structural gate would only restate.

**Verification** — `pnpm verify --list` owns stage membership. Hook, CI, nightly, weekly and pre-push responsibilities
live in `UNIFIED-VERIFICATION-DESIGN.md` §4. Scoped commit checks do not establish whole-tree qualification.

**On-demand lanes** — `pnpm cpd` (jscpd, Layer 5) and `pnpm test:mutation[:gate]` (Stryker, Layer 6).
Enforced — they fail the build — just not in the pre-commit budget.

## Layer 1 — Biome (`biome.json`)

Format + lint + import-organize at `error`, plus four type-aware domains (project/types/react/test) —
see `biome.json` for the exact rule set. `noConsole` is a total ban outside `packages/client/**`
(relaxed until a client logger lands) and `scripts/**`/`tests/**` (console is their output channel).
See `Spine-TypeScript-and-Patterns.md`.

## Layer 2 — ESLint (`eslint.config.js`)

Installed maintained rules own typed, React, accessibility, query, schema and browser API claims
within their proven coverage. Native restrictions own covered import, API and syntax rules.
`eslint.config.js` owns rule selection and scope. Confirm installed behavior and effective configuration
before adding a structural gate or carrying an exception into native configuration.

## Layer 3 — Structural gates (`tooling/src/verify/`, ts-morph + fs)

One module per gate under `gates/`; the loader (`lib/loader.ts`) is the registry — add a gate by
dropping a valid `defineGate` module in that directory, nothing else to register.
`tooling/src/verify/gates/GATE-AUTHORING.md` is the authoring guide; a gate's rule and its reason live
in its own module header, never restated here.

Use a structural gate only for a judgment the compiler and maintained tools cannot express.
Shared code-facts readers own remaining typed analysis; gates and code commands consume the same facts.
The test-foundation plan owns reader migration and native replacement qualification.

Ordinary waiver remediation metadata is validated by `lib/policy-validation.ts` at descriptor admission.

Two deleted gate-local tables are still named here, on purpose, so their `dangling-ref-citations`
reviewed grants stay live: `duplicate-action-doors`'s `EXEMPT_PROCEDURES` (its successor grants name
the open follow-up that must land before this citation can go too) and `density-tier`'s
`ELEVATED_ALLOW` (also named in `UI-Density-Law.md` §5.1).

## Layer 4 — dependency-cruiser (`.dependency-cruiser.cjs`) — active

The import-graph backstop: the package cake, the server tier order, per-feature client isolation, and
the `@orb/inference` seals (the provider credential firewall among them). Every rule states its own
reason in its `comment` — that config is the authority for WHY, never restated here. Scanned via
`pnpm depcruise`; every rule is pinned by `tests/tooling/dependency-cruiser.int.test.ts`. `pnpm knip`
is the separate dead-code/dead-export/dead-dependency lane, live in `pnpm check` as `deps:knip`.

## Layer 5 — jscpd (`jscpd.json`) — copy-paste detection

Scans `packages/**` (TS + TSX + CSS) for structural duplication the per-file rules can't see.
On-demand, not pre-commit: `pnpm cpd` / `pnpm cpd:report`. Gate: 2% duplication threshold.
`pnpm cpd:tests` (`jscpd.tests.json`) scans `tests/` alone with the same settings and holds its duplicated share at
the measured ratchet in that config (Spine-Testing.md §10).

## Layer 6 — Stryker (`stryker.config.js` + `stryker.gate.config.js`) — mutation testing

Mutates source and reruns the suite to score whether tests actually catch bugs, not merely execute the
line. `pnpm test:mutation` (exploratory) and `pnpm test:mutation:gate` (pinned to the highest-stakes
pure modules — chat routing/assembly, credential resolution). On-demand only; `break` stays null in
both configs until a measured score calibrates it.
